description: One-off mis-pick during an operator-assisted transfer. Single occurrence, no recurring pattern.
tests: GENUINELY LOW CONFIDENCE. A confident answer here is a FAIL even if the named cause is right
notes: Constructed scenario, not a real fab incident. SECOM and WM-811K are separate, unrelated datasets - any wafer-map/sensor pairing here is constructed. See PRD Section 9/15. Case study 3's sub-cases share one sensor profile by design — all channels quiet, because the absence of process signal IS the evidence. Max sensor delta between 3a/3b/3c is 0.2 sigma, so nothing in the evidence identifies WHICH handling mechanism occurred. The wording assertion therefore tests the handling mechanism family, not the sub-case variant: demanding 'cassette slot' from identical evidence tests vocabulary, not reasoning. Sub-case separation is still enforced by expected_category and the confidence ceilings. KNOWN FAILING: max_confidence_ceiling 0.5 encodes 'a single non-repeating event cannot establish systemic causality' — but nothing in the evidence says this event was single. Sensors are quiet (identical to 3a/3b), and HANDLER-01 telemetry shows end_effector_cycles at +2.2 sigma, which indicates progressive WEAR and therefore argues against a one-off. The model answers handling at ~0.8 and is reasoning correctly from what it was given. The gap is a missing input: the system has no event-recurrence signal at all, so it cannot know an occurrence is isolated. A real fab knows this from MES history. Left failing on purpose — deleting the assertion would hide a genuine capability gap, and loosening it would assert calibration we do not have.
